categories.main_business_segments: Lamb Weston operates two primary business segments: North America and International. The North America segment covers the U.S., Canada, and Mexico, serving restaurants, foodservice distributors, non-commercial channels, and retailers. The International segment includes operations outside North America, supplying similar customer types globally.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company specializes in the production of value-added frozen potato products, primarily French fries, using advanced processing and packaging technologies. Manufacturing is conducted at 27 facilities worldwide, with a focus on efficiency, food safety, and sustainability, including innovations to reduce waste and water usage. Lamb Weston also leverages proprietary formulations, patented processes, and co-packing arrangements.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Lamb Weston's key customers include quick service and full-service restaurant chains (notably McDonald's, which accounts for 14% of sales), foodservice distributors, non-commercial institutions, and major grocery and mass retail chains. The company serves over 100 countries, with a diverse customer base spanning foodservice, retail, and commercial ingredient markets.
categories.geographic_coverage: Lamb Weston operates in over 100 countries, with production and processing facilities in the U.S., Canada, the Netherlands, Austria, the UK, China, Argentina, and Australia. The company has a strong presence in North America and Europe, and is expanding in high-growth emerging markets such as China and Latin America.
categories.supply_chain_position: Lamb Weston is positioned downstream in the supply chain as a processor and marketer of finished, value-added frozen potato products. The company sources raw potatoes and other inputs from growers and suppliers, processes them into finished goods, and distributes them to foodservice, retail, and institutional customers.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include driving growth through product innovation, expanding global capacity, and enhancing operational efficiency. R&D focuses on new product development, improving product quality, sustainability initiatives (such as reducing water and waste), and supporting customer menu innovation. The company is also investing in digital transformation, including ERP upgrades and supply chain modernization.
categories.revenue_model: Lamb Weston generates revenue primarily through the sale of frozen potato products and appetizers to foodservice, retail, and institutional customers. Revenue is recognized at the point of sale or over time for customized products, with additional income from joint venture service fees and, to a lesser extent, licensing and co-packing arrangements.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include McCain Foods, J.R. Simplot, Cavendish Farms, Aviko, Agristo, Clarebout, Farm Frites, and The Kraft Heinz Company. Lamb Weston is the number one supplier of value-added frozen potato products in North America and a leading global player, competing on product quality, innovation, customer service, and brand strength.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In fiscal 2024, Lamb Weston reported net sales of $6.47 billion, a 21% increase year-over-year, driven by acquisitions and pricing actions. Adjusted EBITDA was $1.42 billion, up 13%. The company has a global workforce of approximately 10,700 employees and continues to invest heavily in capacity expansion and modernization.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Lamb Weston differentiates itself through a broad portfolio of high-quality, innovative frozen potato products, strong customer relationships, and a reputation for reliability and food safety. The company emphasizes its ability to support customer growth, deliver consistent quality, and provide tailored solutions, underpinned by proprietary technologies and a global supply chain.
